math_proof.claim: Per-substrate z-score normalization (with any reference mean mu_ref and std sigma_ref) is a strictly positive-affine transformation per substrate.
math_proof.consequence: Both Pearson r and Spearman r between two paired vectors are INVARIANT under independent positive-affine transformations of each vector.
math_proof.implication: Replacing per-substrate self-z-score with qmirror-reference-z-score MUST yield IDENTICAL Pearson and Spearman r to those already reported in blm_phase5_aligned_exec_2026_05_03/verdict.json. secondary_finding_qmirror_cond6_referenc.issue_1_metric_mismatch: qmirror cond.6 phi_star is computed by pyphi 4.0 sia() MIP-search on a state-by-node TPM (transition probability matrix). anima_phi_v3_canonical (used in BLM Phase 4/5) is covariance-logdet sample-partition phi on hidden activations. The two metrics measure different mathematical objects and are not commensurable as a 'normalization anchor' even if Spearman were not already invariant.
secondary_finding_qmirror_cond6_referenc.issue_2_degenerate_reference: All 4 stored TPMs yield phi_star = 0.0 byte-identical because the marginalized TPM is row-uniform (no causal connectivity in IIT 4.0 sense). A single-point reference (constant 0.0) cannot define a distribution to z-score against (sigma_ref = 0 -> division by zero or undefined z-scores).
secondary_finding_qmirror_cond6_referenc.issue_3_distribution_construction: Generating a 1000-random-circuit qmirror phi distribution would require either (a) running pyphi 4.0 sia() on 1000 small (N<=6) random TPMs (which would still be IIT-4.0-phi values, NOT covariance-logdet phi values, so still incommensurable) or (b) running anima_phi_v3_canonical on hidden states extracted from quantum circuit state vectors -- but quantum state vectors have no concept of a 'sequence of N=16 prompt activations,' so the formula would need to be re-defined.

why_phase5_actually_failed: Phase 5 FAIL is NOT a normalization artifact. It reflects a substantive empirical finding: the anima_phi_v3_canonical formula (covariance-logdet sample-partition phi on top-variance hidden dims) does not transfer between CLM hidden states, EEG fixation-locked epochs, and BOLD HRF-lagged windows -- even when the stimulus is shared (CLM-BOLD pair was true text-shared, n=158, power=0.93 at silver threshold, r_s=-0.058 with CI tight around 0). The phi-formula likely captures substrate-specific covariance structure, not a substrate-invariant 'integration' quantity.

RDMs are invariant to many cross-substrate confounds and are the standard cross-modal alignment tool in cognitive neuroscience (Kriegeskorte 2008). $0 CPU.

ALT-2 (Encoding model): Per-substrate ridge-regression encoding model from CLM hidden states -> EEG/BOLD; cross-validate r per voxel/channel; report mean r across held-out folds. Standard fMRI encoding pipeline (Huth/Gallant 2016). $0 CPU.

ALT-3 (Substrate-matched phi): Re-define phi to be substrate-appropriate per modality -- e.g., complex network phi for EEG (PyPhi on phase-coupling graphs), HRF-deconvolved BOLD before covariance-phi, CLM with longer context windows. Still won't make phi cross-substrate-shared, but at least each substrate has a phi that respects its native dynamics.

honest_c3_caveats: C-Q1: The qmirror cond.6 reference (4 TPMs, all phi_star=0.0) cannot serve as a normalization anchor for cross-substrate phi for two independent reasons: (a) Spearman is invariant to per-substrate affine transforms, so re-normalization cannot change r; (b) qmirror cond.6 phi_star (pyphi sia on TPM) and anima_phi_v3_canonical (cov-logdet on hidden activations) are different mathematical objects.

C-Q2: Even if a NEW canonical anchor were constructed by running anima_phi_v3_canonical on hidden states extracted from 1000 random quantum circuits, this would still constitute an affine renormalization per substrate (mu_ref, sigma_ref are constants per substrate), so Spearman invariance still kills the proposed F-QCAL-1 silver recovery. The only way phi normalization could change Spearman is via a NON-MONOTONIC transformation, which would fundamentally alter the meaning of phi.
C-Q3: Phase 5 FAIL is empirically robust at adequate power (CLM-BOLD n=158, power=0.93). The genuine null is not a 'normalization mistake' artifact -- it is the answer the experiment delivered.
